extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, peer reviewers, and researchers studying peer review practices (psychology)
extracted.subtask_description: An operational coding scheme of the grounds psychology reviewers actually used to reject manuscripts (from Peters & Ceci 1982), plus inferred reviewer-quality norms and editor recommendations to improve fairness and rigor in peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serious methodological flaws
rubrics_metrics.description: Design, sampling, controls inadequate to draw the reported conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers core experimental or observational design problems that undermine validity. Examples/anti-patterns: absent or inappropriate control groups, poor randomization, flawed operationalizations that prevent valid inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Wrong tests, inadequate power, multiple comparisons, ignored assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes misuse of statistical methods (e.g., inappropriate tests), failure to account for multiple comparisons, low statistical power, and ignoring assumptions (normality, independence). Reviewers flag these as rendering analyses unreliable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadequate / inappropriate sample
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition or size of the sample is insufficient or unsuitable for the claims made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concerns about sample representativeness, small N, biased sampling, or demographic mismatches relative to generalizations. Guidance: critique should connect sample limitations to limits on inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to consider alternative explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Confounds, third variables, and plausible rival explanations are not addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers penalize manuscripts that do not rule out confounds or fail to discuss plausible alternative mechanisms. Good reviews identify what additional analyses or designs would distinguish alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weak or implausible theoretical rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: The research question is uninteresting, poorly motivated, or the framing is muddled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticisms target the conceptual grounding: weak hypotheses, lack of theoretical novelty, or unclear linkage between theory and method. Guidance: reviewers should specify why the rationale is weak and what stronger framing would look like.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient practical or theoretical contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if competent, the manuscript does not advance the field enough to merit publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations of 'importance' or 'contribution' often conflate with methodological soundness; guidance is to separate these judgments and justify claims about contribution relative to the literature and journal scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to control for relevant variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Important confounding or relevant variables have not been measured or controlled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinct from general methodological flaws, this specifically points to omitted controls. Reviewers should indicate which variables are missing and how their absence affects conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadequate literature review
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical prior work is overlooked or misrepresented in the manuscript's background and positioning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes ignoring key studies, mischaracterizing prior findings, or failing to situate the work in the field. Good reviews point to specific missing references and explain the impact on novelty/claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poor quality of writing / presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization, clarity, and exposition are insufficient for evaluating or understanding the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problems include unclear prose, poor structure, ambiguous descriptions of methods/results, and formatting issues. Guidance: distinguish presentation problems that can be fixed from substantive flaws that warrant rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inferences not warranted by the data
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors draw conclusions that the data do not support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers overgeneralization, causal claims from correlational data, and speculative leaps. Reviewers should indicate which inferences are unsupported and what evidence would be required to justify them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make explicit what evidence would change the evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should state what specific evidence or analyses would alter their judgement, otherwise their judgements are unfalsifiable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescriptive norm: reviews should include counterfactuals or acceptance conditions (e.g., 'If authors provided X analysis or controlled for Y, I would reconsider'). This enhances transparency and constructiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish importance from methodological soundness
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should separate judgements about the manuscript's importance/significance from judgements about methodological rigor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conflating 'not important' with 'methodologically flawed.' Provide distinct reasoning and criteria for significance versus soundness so editors can weigh trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be alert to status / institutional bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should avoid letting author prestige or institutional affiliation influence their evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peters & Ceci demonstrated identical work received different critiques when credited to low-status institutions. Guidance: reviewers and editors should acknowledge potential halo effects and aim for objective criterion-based assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider double-blind review to reduce institutional halo
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should consider implementing double-blind review to mitigate prestige-based bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial policy recommendation: conceal author identities/affiliations during review. Guidance includes calibrating process and training to ensure blinding is effective where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibrate against the journal's published acceptance criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should align their recommendations with the journal's stated acceptance standards, since the same article had previously met them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescriptive: reviewers should reference the journal's aims/scope and explicit criteria when justifying major concerns, and editors should ensure reviewers are aware of these standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicitly state disciplinary norms being invoked
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should specify which disciplinary norms or standards they rely on, rather than appealing to vague 'standards.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit whether objections are methodological, theoretical, ethical, or normative and cite community norms, guidelines, or precedents. This helps authors and editors interpret and act on reviews.
